claims.text: Homogenization followed by controlled aging of Al0.5CoCrFeNi will induce L12-phase precipitation.
The induced L12 precipitates will be fine and coherent with the FCC matrix.
The proposed treatment will improve yield strength by approximately 25%.
The proposed treatment will enhance fracture resistance.
The proposed treatment will preserve ductility.
The proposed treatment will preserve Young's modulus.
The initial homogenized Al0.5CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase FCC material with minimal elemental segregation.
Homogenization at approximately 1100 °C eliminates microsegregation in Al0.5CoCrFeNi.
Aging at 600 °C for 8–12 hours produces a uniform distribution of nanoscale, coherent L12 precipitates in a ductile FCC matrix.
Inert or vacuum processing is necessary to prevent oxidation during the treatment.
Excessive aging can cause precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency.
The approach is expected to work only when the initial alloy is well homogenized and lacks significant segregation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces minimize stress concentrations and therefore maintain ductility.
A controlled precipitate distribution arrests crack propagation and enhances fracture resistance.
The precipitate distribution will not significantly alter Young's modulus.
Conventionally processed state-of-the-art Al0.5CoCrFeNi alloys have lower yield strength than the proposed treated alloy.
Conventionally processed state-of-the-art Al0.5CoCrFeNi alloys have lower fracture resistance while possessing similar ductility and Young's modulus.
The expected benefits may disappear if the precipitates exceed the nanoscale regime or lose coherency.
The quantitative mechanical benefits depend on processing deviations and precipitation kinetics in the high-entropy alloy.
